mapping.rust: pub enum Tree<A> { Leaf, Node(Box<Tree<A>>, A, Box<Tree<A>>) }
mapping.basis: Tree_Test.tree has exactly the constructors Leaf (nullary) and Node (left subtree, value, right subtree); the Rust enum preserves this structure with boxed recursive children.
conditions: The type parameter A is arbitrary and unconstrained.
Node field order is left subtree, value, right subtree.
Box is used only to make the recursive Rust type finite.

mapping.basis: Tree_Test.tree.Leaf is the nullary constructor of Tree_Test.tree, represented by the nullary Rust enum variant.
conditions: It inhabits Tree<A> for any A.

mapping.basis: Tree_Test.tree.Node is the ternary datatype constructor with fields tree, 'a, tree; the Rust tuple variant has the same field order.
conditions: Arguments are left subtree, value, right subtree.
Recursive child trees are owned boxed values.

mapping.rust: pub fn mirror<A>(t: Tree<A>) -> Tree<A> { match t { Tree::Leaf => Tree::Leaf, Tree::Node(l, x, r) => { let mirrored_right = mirror(*r); let mirrored_left = mirror(*l); Tree::Node(Box::new(mirrored_right), x, Box::new(mirrored_left)) } } }
mapping.basis: The source equations are mirror Leaf = Leaf and mirror (Node l x r) = Node (mirror r) x (mirror l); the Rust match implements exactly these two cases and preserves the recursive source route.
conditions: Consumes the input tree by value.
Recursively mirrors the right subtree, then the left, and stores them in swapped positions.
No Clone, Copy, numeric, or ordering bounds are introduced.
